run.final_diagnosis:
When no credentials are supplied by the application on the createConnection call, WebSphere Application Server provides a blank username to MQ, causing the connection to use the administrative user 'mqm' on UNIX/Linux systems and 'MUSR_MQADMIN' on Windows. This explains why the configured credentials are not being used and the sys admin user is used instead. [1]
To select the intended outbound identity, configure the component-managed authentication alias using wsadmin scripting. For JACL, use the command: wsadmin>$AdminTask modifyWMQConnectionFactory MyCF(cells/mycell|resources.xml#MQConnectionFactory_1247500675104) { -componentAuthAlias myalias } [1]
If it is impractical to change the application to use container-managed security or to supply a username and password directly on the createConnection call, the component-managed authentication alias can be configured to use the intended outbound identity. [1]
The configured credentials are not being used because the application server is providing a blank username, which defaults to the administrative user 'mqm' or 'MUSR_MQADMIN'. This is why the same MQ service works fine in the old BPM environment but not in the new one. [1]

attempts.diagnosis:
Default behaviour when no credentials are supplied in the application server 

If no credentials are supplied by the application on the createConnection call, and neither of the component managed or container managed security systems described below are configured, then WebSphere Application Server provides a blank username to MQ. This causes MQ to authorise the client based on the userid that the MQ listener is running under. In the majority of cases this is 'mqm' on UNIX/Linux systems and 'MUSR_MQADMIN' on Windows. 

As these are administrative MQ users, they will be blocked by default in WebSphere MQ V7.1 and higher, with a AMQ9777 error logged in the error logs of the queue manager.

Default container-managed authentication alias for outbound connections 

For cases where it is impractical to change the application to use container-managed security, or to change it to supply a username and password directly on the createConnection call, it is possible to supply a default. 

This default is called the "container-managed authentication alias" and cannot be configured via the administrative console (since WebSphere Application Server Version 7.0 when it was removed from the panels MQ connection factories). The below scripting samples show how to configure it using wsadmin: 

 * JACL:
   wsadmin>set cell [ $AdminConfig getid "/Cell:mycell" ]
   
   mycell(cells/mycell|cell.xml#Cell_1)
   
   wsadmin>$AdminTask listWMQConnectionFactories $cell
   
   MyCF(cells/mycell|resources.xml#MQConnectionFactory_1247500675104)
   
   wsadmin>$AdminTask modifyWMQConnectionFactory MyCF(cells/mycell|resources.xml#MQConnectionFactory_1247500675104) { -containerAuthAlias myalias }
   
   MyCF(cells/mycell|resources.xml#MQConnectionFactory_1247500675104) 
 * Jython:
   wsadmin>cell = AdminConfig.getid("/Cell:mycell")

If it is impractical to change the application to use container-managed security or to supply a username and password directly on the createConnection call, the component-managed authentication alias can be configured to use the intended outbound identity. [1]
